doc.title: Bob Cranshaw interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

chapter: Sesame Street and playing for feel
title: Working with Raposo and drummer Danny Epstein; Billy Taylor at night
summary: He kept Raposo's bass-note playing intact, enjoyed Danny Epstein's feel, sent Walter Booker in as a sub, and played with Billy Taylor at night.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: You had the ability to diagnose, at speed, on the spot.

Yeah. I can hear and I know that that bass is important. We need, bass players are very important. But I didn’t want to change, he didn’t play, he played the pump and he was always playing the bass note. But I didn’t mind. I could hear what he was doing, and as long as I could hear it, you know, I said look, why disturb what he was doing? It’s okay. If we play the same note it’s okay. I don’t mind that. But it’s going to feel good. I’m going to make the note that he played, it’s going to feel so good to him. He’s going to enjoy playing it. And so I was not only playing different music but I was in with a different group of guys than I would ordinarily work, I would probably never have worked with a Joe Raposo or the drummer Danny Epstein. And we had a trio. We started to work, and then I got into Sesame Street with Joe Raposo playing and a guy named Danny Epstein. I had never played with a drummer who played, I mean after playing with the Art Taylors and the Philly Jo Jones and the Mickey Rokers and so forth, I started to play with this guy Danny Epstein. And I used to, he was a Jewish guy from Forest Hills. And we would play a tune and I’d tell him to play “Forest Hills Rock” you know he was always asking me well how should I play this? I’d say just play “Forest Hills Rock.” Just play what you play. But he had such a wonderful feeling too. We just had a blend. And we enjoyed each other. We would come in and we’d play and we would laugh. And I started to send other bass players when I started to work Sesame Street after a while, I’d

send in Walter Booker and a lot of other guys who also enjoyed the experience that I was having working with this group of guys. I would do this during the day and at night I was working with Billy Taylor. So I got the chance to enjoy all of it. I had my cake and I ate it too.
